name: Stable-only standalone updater

core: Stable-only release policy and immutable exact-plan selection.
Checksum pinned during Prepare, then checksum-before-extract, bounded staging, and strict non-mutating staged and installed version verification during Apply.
Per-target locking, no-clobber backup, replacement, rollback, and UI-neutral progress events.

adapters.role: Public GitHub Releases implementation of the release Source port.
Strict command-based version verifier for released executables.

host: Provide current-version truth, executable path, release/archive naming, and strict version output mapping.
Select the supported install-kind adapter before invoking a transaction.
Enforce authorization and render progress in the product's own channel.
Own restart, post-restart acknowledgement, discovery cadence, and failure UX.
excludes: Cards, buttons, chat commands, natural-language intent, localization, or administrator UI.
Host process restart or post-restart messaging.
Beta or nightly channel policy in the ordinary stable updater.
npm, Homebrew, or Windows replacement guarantees in the standalone updater.

prerequisites: Stable GitHub Releases use exact semantic-version tags and contain an archive plus checksums.txt.
The released binary has a strict, non-mutating version probe.
The host can enforce update authorization and owns restart behavior.
invariants: Ordinary update flows accept only exact stable tags matching v?X.Y.Z.
Prepare selects the exact release and assets, downloads its checksum manifest, and returns an opaque plan.
Apply installs only that plan and never resolves latest again; a later successful Prepare supersedes older plans.
The checksum manifest and archive are exact assets on the same selected Release, and the pinned SHA-256 cannot move between confirmation and Apply.
SHA-256 is verified before archive extraction or executable mutation.
The staged binary reports the selected version before replacement and the version probe cannot change its content.
The old executable is backed up through a no-clobber same-filesystem link and never overwrites a pre-existing backup.
The installed binary reports the selected version without changing its content after replacement, or the old executable is restored.
Concurrent operations on one updater or target serialize, while unrelated target paths remain independent.
Executable and lock-file symlinks are refused by the standalone updater.
GitHub API and asset redirects cannot downgrade from HTTPS, including with a host-provided HTTP client.
Core update policy contains no chat, CLI, localization, or restart presentation logic.
integration_steps: Inventory current-version truth, release assets, executable path, version output, all update entry points, authorization, and restart lifecycle.
Configure one updater.Updater plus updater/github.Source with the exact repository, archive naming function, static or release-derived archive binary name, and strict version verifier.
Route chat, CLI, UI, and manual update actions to that same updater service instead of duplicating installers.
For interactive flows call Prepare, render Plan.Release and Plan.ArchiveAsset, obtain authorization, then call Apply with that exact Plan.
Use UpdateLatest only for an already-authorized non-interactive CLI or administrator action.
Render updater.Event values in each adapter without branching update policy.
Keep beta/nightly installation separate and never feed prereleases into the stable updater.
After a successful transaction, let the host perform its graceful restart and post-restart acknowledgement.
Add failure-injection tests for checksum, staged version, installed version rollback, and concurrency.
